timing: retrospective specification of previously generated candidate

sourceFacts.fact: Most Down syndrome results from three copies of chromosome21.
Other forms involve translocation or mosaicism, so this diagram specifically depicts free trisomy.

invariants: Exactly two versus three separated matching chromosome icons.
Only common free-trisomy form; not diagnostic karyotype morphology.
expectedLabels: The common free-trisomy form of Down syndrome
layoutSpecification: Two clear chromosome-count groups on warm ivory background. Title 'Trisomy 21: an extra copy'. Left heading 'Two copies': EXACTLY TWO small matching acrocentric chromosome21 symbols, each with a tiny short arm above high centromere and long arms below; both muted teal. Right heading 'Three copies': EXACTLY THREE matching chromosome21 symbols; two muted teal and third pale ochre. Label below each group 'Chromosome 21'. Bottom 'The common free-trisomy form of Down syndrome'. No full karyotype, no infant faces, no physically different third chromosome, no duplicated chromosome arms miscounted as chromosomes. Small subtitle 'Copy-number schematic'. All chromosome symbols same size and shape, distinct separated silhouettes.
forbiddenAnatomy: No claimed anatomical reconstruction, diagnostic image, histology or literal neuroanatomical pathway
No organ cutaways or invented internal spatial relationships

validation.sourceFacts: Checked against listed primary clinical sources during original topic review
validation.pixelChecks: Explicit structure check: exactly two chromosome21 symbols in comparison group and three in trisomy group, same shapes with one additional highlighted copy; caption limits claim to common free trisomy. This verifies copy-count logic only, not a diagnostic karyotype.
